audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer says his 'Q bite steals your AD and heals him' (whys[0], early). Chomp does not heal.
audit.why: Chomp damages, briefly slows and saps attack damage. The healing comes from two other places: King's Tribute heals him whenever a nearby unit dies — which is every minion in the wave — and Frozen Domain increases the healing he receives from all sources. Blaming the bite for the sustain sends the player to dodge the wrong thing.
audit.corrected: Chomp saps AD on a 3.5s cooldown; King's Tribute is the wave-based heal; Frozen Domain amplifies all of it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json — P, Q and W descriptions

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer connects Chomp to Siphoning Strike specifically.
audit.why: Siphoning Strike scales off attack damage. Chomp is the only ability in this matchup that removes attack damage, and it is on a 3.5 second cooldown at every rank, so he can hold the debuff on Nasus almost permanently. That is a direct tax on the one number Nasus spends the whole game growing, and it is why the bite feels worse than its damage.
audit.corrected: Every Chomp shaves damage off the next empowered Q; it is up every 3.5s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Pillar of Ice is described in the content layer only as a body-block, and never appears in the full layer at all.
audit.why: It creates impassable terrain. Nasus has no dash anywhere in his kit, so a Pillar dropped between him and Trundle ends the chase outright — there is no ability that gets him past it. That makes Pillar, not Subjugate, the cooldown that decides whether Nasus ever gets to spend his stacks. It is 21/19.5/18/16.5/15s.
audit.corrected: Pillar of Ice is the real punish window: wait for it to be spent before committing to a chase.
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json — E Pillar of Ice, terrain flag
champ-data/_kits/nasus.json — no dash flag in kit

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns tracked Subjugate, a 120s ultimate, as the matchup-defining cooldown and gave no numbers.
audit.why: The lane is decided by Pillar of Ice and Chomp, not by an ultimate that comes up twice a lane phase.
audit.corrected: Replaced with Pillar of Ice per-rank numbers plus the Subjugate rank-1 number.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds named anywhere, and the winCon string literally says "Anti-heal" without ever telling the player what to buy or when.
audit.why: King's Tribute heals a percentage of the maximum health of every unit that dies near him, and Frozen Domain increases healing from all sources while he stands on it. Against a Nasus whose win condition is a long lifesteal grind, unanswered healing amplification is the loss condition.
audit.corrected: Frozen Domain called out as a healing amplifier in dosFull[2] and phases[2]; the actual item timing still needs a home in the itemization block, which lives in report[].
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json — P and W heal flags

audit.whatIsWrong: This is the most mislabelled matchup in the slice: diff=HARD, diffRating=7/10, and the full chart gives Trundle stages 1-5 at 8/10 — for a matchup Nasus wins 56.63%, the highest win rate in this slice.
audit.why: The content layer already says the opposite ("This is your game", Nasus on stages 4-7). Trundle is a melee drain tank with no true damage and no percent-health shred, which is the exact profile Nasus out-scales.
audit.corrected: Should read EVEN 6/10 at worst, with Trundle holding only stage 1. Not edited: "Trundle" is 7 characters against "Nasus"/"Skill" at 5, so every side flip fails the ±10% band, and diff/diffRating cannot be changed without also changing the report[] rating string.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flagged "Spirit Fire's" in spikes[3] as a probable wrong ability name.
audit.why: False positive — Spirit Fire is Nasus's E.

notes: Trundle is the clearest example of the champion-wide difficulty-label drift: 56.63% win rate labelled HARD 7/10 with the enemy holding five of seven stages, while the content layer on the same page says Nasus owns it. Sample is only 249 games, the smallest in this slice, but the direction is not in doubt.
